_comment: Drills as vertices of the graph. The key is the drill's id (d1, d2, ...): assigned once, never reused, the way LeetCode numbers are; it is what "after" lists, make prepare and make next use. "title" is what make next, make rep and the commit show; nothing reads it from a file. "file" is the bank file, relative to drills/: the one place an id meets its file. A rep's evidence entry carries the id as "drill" (written by make solved from .drill.json, 2026-10-24); the reps are found by that, never by the title or a filename. "after": [ids] - what this drill builds on; an id is a drill id, a problem number, or a node id, and the drill is not served until each is warm (kg_lib.warm). Filename order means nothing. Seeded 2026-08-31 from the bank's former filename order. "trains" is the list of node ids the drill evidences; it lives here, keyed by the stable id, so a node rename never touches a bank file or a solved copy. "judge" (optional) is the part of the drill's contract that names the solution: the members, steps, conditions or failure mode the rep must show. The judge reads it (kg_extract drill_lead); the reader never does, because the statement's REQUIRED line carries only the complexity bound and the bans (2026-11-05).

d19.title: Multi-Buy
d19.judge: `term` never touches a digit: every part is fetched by calling self.atom(). `term` claims only '*' and '/': it stops the moment it sees '+', '-' or the end of the string, and leaves that character unread. Consuming it makes the multi-buy swallow the rest of the order.

d20.title: Longest Run of Ones
d20.judge: Two pointers; left advances at most once per element read (an if, never a while). A plain streak counter passes the asserts while skipping the slide, and the slide is the rep: it is the fail.

d21.title: Slide, Never Shrink
d21.judge: left advances at most once per element read and the width never decreases. Shrinking back to a legal window on every step is the fail: it is the shape of Grow and Shrink, and means the drill was not attempted.

d22.title: Fixed Slide
d22.judge: The window's counts are maintained across the slide: one character enters on the right and one leaves on the left, each in O(1). Rebuilding the summary per window is the fail; len(s) makes O(n*k) a TLE. A plain dict, or dsa/sliding_window.py, is fine.

d24.title: Grow and Shrink
d24.judge: Both ends of the window move forward only. The counts are maintained by one add and one remove. Measuring a window that is not legal is the fail: the answers come back too large.

d25.title: Shrink While Valid
d25.judge: Both ends of the window move forward only. The counts are maintained by one add and one remove. A legal window can hold a shorter legal window inside it, so measuring a window the moment it first becomes legal is the fail: the lengths come back too large.

d330.title: Basic Regex Parser

d351.judge: A set of the values; for each y in arr order the pair exists when y + k is in the set; k == 0 returns [] before any lookup.

d352.title: Pancake Sort
d352.judge: For each end from the last index down: the index of the largest element in the prefix, one flip to bring it to the front, one flip to send it to end.

d353.title: Root of Number
d353.judge: Bisection on the answer interval, whose upper bound is max(1, x) so that x below 1 works, halving until the interval is narrower than the tolerance.

d354.title: Sales Path
d354.judge: A leaf returns its own cost; an inner node returns its cost plus the minimum of its children's returns. One call per node.

d355.title: Sentence Reverse
d355.judge: The whole list is reversed in place, then each word is reversed in place by a converging swap between its two ends.

d356.title: Sentence Similarity
d356.judge: A union-find over words: each pair unions its two words, and the sentences are similar when every index pair shares a root.

d357.title: Shifted Array Search
d357.judge: At each step one half is sorted; num is placed in or out of that half by comparing with its two ends, and the other half is kept otherwise.

d358.title: Shortest Word Edit Path
d358.judge: A queue of (word, steps) seeded with source; neighbours come from replacing one letter with each lowercase letter and testing membership in the word set, which drops a word when it is first reached.

d359.title: Smallest Substring of All Characters
d359.judge: A Counter of the wanted characters inside the window grows at the right end; while every wanted character is present the window is recorded and shrunk from the left.

d360.title: Sudoku Solver
d360.judge: Nine sets per row, per column and per box, seeded from the given digits (a clash among them returns False at once); the blanks are listed once and filled in order, a digit is added to the three sets and the cell before the recursive call and removed after it fails.

d361.title: Time Planner
d361.judge: Two indices, one per list. The overlap of the current pair is max of starts to min of ends; the index whose slot ends first advances.

d362.title: Toeplitz Matrix
d362.judge: Every cell at row r >= 1 and column c >= 1 is compared with the cell at (r - 1, c - 1); any mismatch is False.

d363.title: Validate IP Address
d363.judge: The string is split on '.' into exactly four parts; each part is all ASCII digits, is '0' or has no leading '0', and converts to at most 255.

d364.title: Word Count Engine
d364.judge: A Counter over lowercased, letters-only tokens, then buckets indexed by count read from the largest count down; the ties keep first-appearance order because the Counter keeps insertion order.

d365.title: Rank One Players
d365.judge: A plain WHERE on the stored rank column: rank = 1.

d366.title: Top Player Per Team
d366.judge: The query of d149 (dense_rank partitioned by team, by points descending) is named in a WITH clause, and the query of d365 (rank = 1) reads from it. A WHERE on the window alias in the same query is the failure.

d367.title: EPI 4.1 Computing the parity of a word
d367.judge: XOR folds the word onto itself: x ^= x >> 32, then 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1. Bit 0 then holds the XOR of all 64 bits, and x & 1 is the answer.

d368.title: EPI 4.2 Swap bits
d368.judge: The bits change only when they differ: (x >> i) & 1 != (x >> j) & 1. Then one XOR with the mask (1 << i) | (1 << j) flips both bits.

d369.title: EPI 4.3 Reverse bits
d369.judge: The constructor fills a table of the reversed value of each 16-bit number, from the entry for i >> 1. A call takes the four 16-bit groups of x from the low end and puts their reversed values into the result from the high end.

d370.title: EPI 4.4 Find a closest integer with the same weight
d370.judge: Find the lowest index i where bit i and bit i + 1 differ, and swap those two bits with x ^ (0b11 << i). A swap at a higher index changes x by more.

d371.title: EPI 4.5 Compute product without arithmetical operators
d371.judge: Addition is a loop: a ^ b is the sum without carries, (a & b) << 1 is the carry, and the loop stops when the carry is 0. Multiplication adds y shifted left by k for each set bit k of x.

d372.title: EPI 4.6 Compute quotient without arithmetical operators
d372.judge: Find the largest shift such that y << shift <= x. Then go down from that shift to 0: when y << shift <= x, subtract it from x and add 1 << shift to the quotient.

d373.title: EPI 4.7 Compute pow(x,y)
d373.judge: Exponentiation by squaring: a negative y becomes 1 / x and -y. For each bit of y from the low end, the result takes the current x when the bit is 1, and x is squared.

d374.title: EPI 4.8 Reverse digits
d374.judge: Work on abs(x): divmod by 10 takes off the last digit, and result * 10 + digit appends it. The sign of x goes back on at the end.

d375.title: EPI 4.9 Check if a decimal integer is a palindrome
d375.judge: A negative x is False. A power of 10 with the same digit count as x gives the first digit by x // high, and x % 10 gives the last. Compare them, remove both with x % high // 10, and divide high by 100.

d376.title: EPI 4.10 Generate uniform random numbers
d376.judge: Rejection sampling: build r from the bits of zero_one_random() until 2^bits >= n, the number of values. Use lower_bound + r when r < n, else draw again.

d377.title: EPI 4.11 Rectangle intersection
d377.judge: The intersection has x = max of the left edges, y = max of the bottom edges, and width and height = min of the far edges minus those. A negative width or height means no intersection.

d378.title: EPI 5.1 The Dutch national flag problem
d378.judge: Three indices split A into less, equal, unknown and greater regions. An element less than the pivot is swapped to the front of the unknown region and both front indices advance; an equal element only advances the scan index; a greater element is swapped with the last unknown element and the back index moves left without advancing the scan.

d379.title: EPI 5.2 Increment an arbitrary-precision integer
d379.judge: Scan from the last digit toward the first: each 9 becomes 0 and the carry moves left; the first digit that is not 9 is increased by 1 and the scan stops. When every digit was 9, the first digit becomes 1 and a 0 is appended.

d380.title: EPI 5.3 Multiply two arbitrary-precision integers
d380.judge: The sign is taken from the two first digits and the work is done on absolute values. A result list of len(num1) + len(num2) zeros receives each product num1[i] * num2[j] at position i + j + 1, with the carry pushed to position i + j at once. Leading zeros are removed, keeping at least the last digit, and the sign is applied to the first digit.

d381.title: EPI 5.4 Advancing through an array
d381.judge: A single left-to-right scan keeps the furthest index reachable so far as the maximum of i + A[i]. The scan returns False as soon as the current index is past that furthest index; otherwise the end is reachable.

d382.title: EPI 5.5 Delete duplicates from a sorted array
d382.judge: A write index marks the end of the distinct prefix. Each read element is copied to the write index only when it differs from the last written element (or nothing is written yet), and the write index is then advanced; its final value is the count returned.

d383.title: EPI 5.6 Buy and sell a stock once
d383.judge: A single scan keeps the minimum price seen so far and the best profit so far, updating the best with the current price minus that minimum.

d384.title: EPI 5.7 Buy and sell a stock twice
d384.judge: A forward pass stores, for each day, the best single-trade profit that sells before that day, from a running minimum. A backward pass keeps a running maximum and the best single-trade profit that buys on or after the day, and the answer is the best sum of the stored forward value and the backward value at the same split day.

d385.title: EPI 5.8 Computing an alternation
d385.judge: A single left-to-right scan over adjacent pairs swaps A[i - 1] and A[i] when the pair breaks the required direction for index i: less-or-equal when i is odd, greater-or-equal when i is even. A swap never breaks the pair before it.

d386.title: EPI 5.9 Enumerate all primes to n
d386.judge: A boolean table for 0 to n starts true from 2 upward. For each i up to the square root of n whose entry is still true, every multiple of i from i * i to n is set false. The indices still true are returned.

d387.title: EPI 5.10 Permute the elements of an array
d387.judge: Each index i is processed until perm[i] == i: the element at i is swapped to its target j = perm[i], and perm[i] and perm[j] are swapped as well, so perm[j] becomes j and position i receives the next element of the cycle with its own target. Every swap fixes one element, so the total work is linear.

d388.title: EPI 5.11 Compute the next permutation
d388.judge: Scan from the right for the first index i with perm[i] < perm[i + 1]; if there is none, return []. Swap perm[i] with the rightmost element greater than it, then reverse the suffix after i with two pointers that move toward each other, which turns the decreasing suffix into increasing order.

d389.title: EPI 5.12 Sample offline data
d389.judge: For i from 0 to k - 1, pick a random index j from i to len(A) - 1 and swap A[i] with A[j]. The prefix A[:i] is the sample built so far, and each step draws uniformly from the elements not yet chosen (a partial Fisher-Yates shuffle).

d390.title: EPI 5.13 Sample online data
d390.judge: The first k elements fill the sample. For the n-th element after that, draw a random integer j in [0, n): when j < k, the element replaces sample[j]; otherwise it is dropped. Each element is read once and the stream is never stored.

d391.title: EPI 5.14 Compute a random permutation
d391.judge: Start from the list 0 to n - 1. For each i, swap position i with a random index from i to n - 1 (Fisher-Yates). Drawing the index from the whole list instead of from i onward gives a biased result.

d392.title: EPI 5.15 Compute a random subset
d392.judge: Run the first k steps of a Fisher-Yates shuffle over a virtual list 0 to n - 1 held in a dict: a key that is absent stands for its own value. Each step draws j from i to n - 1 and swaps the values at i and j through the dict, and the values at keys 0 to k - 1 are returned.

d393.title: EPI 5.16 Generate nonuniform random numbers
d393.judge: Build the running sums of the probabilities, so value i owns the interval from the previous sum to its own sum. Draw a uniform float in [0, total) and return the value whose interval holds it, found by a right-side binary search over the running sums; intervals of length 0 are never hit.

d394.title: EPI 5.17 The Sudoku checker problem
d394.judge: A single pass over the 81 cells records, for every nonzero digit, a key for its row, its column and its subgrid (i // 3, j // 3) in a set. A key that is already in the set is a repeat, and the answer is False at once.

d395.title: EPI 5.18 Compute the spiral ordering of a 2D array
d395.judge: Process the matrix layer by layer with two bounds lo and hi: read the top row, the right column, the bottom row in reverse and the left column in reverse, each side stopping before the corner the next side starts at. Move both bounds inward. For odd n the center element is added at the end.

d396.title: EPI 5.19 Rotate a 2D array
d396.judge: Transpose the matrix in place by swapping each element above the main diagonal with its mirror below it, then reverse each row. Together the two steps move the element at (i, j) to (j, n - 1 - i). Swapping the four elements of each ring cycle is also correct.

d397.title: EPI 5.20 Compute rows in Pascal's Triangle
d397.judge: Build the rows in order. Each row i starts as i + 1 ones, and each inner element j is the sum of elements j - 1 and j of the previous row.

d398.title: EPI 6.1 Interconvert strings and integers
d398.judge: int_to_string takes the sign apart, then repeats divmod by 10 and maps each remainder to a character with chr(ord('0') + d), collecting the digits least significant first and reversing them at the end; zero still gives "0". string_to_int skips a leading sign and folds the digits left to right as n * 10 + digit, then applies the sign.

d399.title: EPI 6.2 Base conversion
d399.judge: Read the digits left to right into an integer with n * b1 + digit, using a digit string or map for 'A' to 'F'. Then write n in base b2 by repeated divmod, digits collected least significant first and reversed, with 0 giving "0" and the '-' put back in front.

d400.title: EPI 6.3 Compute the spreadsheet column encoding
d400.judge: Treat the id as a base-26 number whose digits run from 1 to 26 instead of 0 to 25: fold left to right as n * 26 + (ord(c) - ord('A') + 1).

d401.title: EPI 6.4 Replace and remove
d401.judge: A forward pass with a read index and a write index drops each 'b' and counts the 'a's. The final length is the kept length plus the count of 'a's. A backward pass then copies from the last kept character to the final end, writing 'd', 'd' for each 'a', so no write overtakes an unread character.

d402.title: EPI 6.5 Test palindromicity
d402.judge: Two indices start at the two ends and move toward each other. Each step skips a character that is not alphanumeric on either side; otherwise it compares the two characters with lower() and moves both inward, returning False on the first mismatch and True when the indices meet.

d403.title: EPI 6.6 Reverse all the words in a sentence
d403.judge: Reverse the whole list with a swap helper on a range, then walk the list and reverse each maximal run of non-space characters back to its original order. The space runs need no second reversal because they are made of equal characters.

d404.title: EPI 6.7 The look-and-say problem
d404.judge: Start from "1" and repeat n - 1 times: walk the current term, find each maximal group of equal digits with an inner index, append the group length and the digit to a list, and join the list into the next term.

d405.title: EPI 6.8 Convert from Roman to decimal
d405.judge: Map each symbol to its value. Start the total with the value of the last symbol and walk the earlier symbols: subtract a value that is smaller than the value of the symbol to its right, add it otherwise.

d406.title: EPI 6.9 Compute all valid IP addresses
d406.judge: Choose the three dot positions with three nested loops, each part 1 to 3 characters long, so at most 27 splits are tried whatever the length of s. A part is valid when it is "0" or has no leading zero, and its value is at most 255. Join the four parts with '.' when all are valid.

d407.title: EPI 6.10 Write a string sinusoidally
d407.judge: The row of s[i] depends only on i mod 4: the top row holds indices 1, 5, 9, ..., the middle row the even indices, the bottom row 3, 7, 11, .... Emit the three index sequences in that order, with strided slices or with range steps of 4, 2 and 4.

d408.title: EPI 6.11 Implement run-length encoding
d408.judge: encoding walks the string, finds each maximal run of equal letters with an inner index and appends str(run length) + letter. decoding accumulates the digits into a count with count * 10 + digit and, at each letter, appends the letter count times and resets the count to 0. Both join a list at the end.

d409.title: EPI 6.12 Find the first occurrence of a substring
d409.judge: Compute a polynomial hash of s and of the first window of t, modulo a large prime. Slide the window by one position at a time, removing the outgoing character with the precomputed base ** (len(s) - 1) and adding the incoming one. When the two hashes are equal, confirm with a direct comparison before returning the index. An empty pattern returns 0 and a pattern longer than t returns -1.

d410.title: EPI 7.1 Merge two sorted lists
d410.judge: A dummy head and a tail pointer; while both lists have nodes, splice the smaller head onto the tail and advance that list, then attach the rest of the list that is left.

d411.title: EPI 7.2 Reverse a single sublist
d411.judge: Walk a pointer from a dummy head to the node before position start, reverse the next finish - start + 1 nodes, and link the reversed run back between the node before it and the node after it.

d412.title: EPI 7.3 Test for cyclicity
d412.judge: Move slow by one node and fast by two until they meet or fast reaches None; after a meeting, restart slow at head and move both by one node, and the node where they meet again is the first node of the cycle.

d413.title: EPI 7.4 Test for overlapping lists - lists are cycle-free
d413.judge: Count the length of each list, advance the head of the longer list by the difference, then move both pointers together until they are the same node or None.

d414.title: EPI 7.5 Test for overlapping lists - lists may have cycles
d414.judge: Find the first cycle node of each list with Floyd's method; no cycle in either list uses the length-difference walk, a cycle in only one list means no common node, and with two cycles walk around the first cycle to see if it reaches the cycle node of the second.

d415.title: EPI 7.6 Delete a node from a singly linked list
d415.judge: Copy the value of the next node into node_to_delete, then set its next to the node after the next node.

d416.title: EPI 7.7 Remove the kth last element from a list
d416.judge: Advance a lead pointer k nodes, start a trailing pointer at a dummy head, move both until the lead pointer is None, then unlink the node after the trailing pointer.

d417.title: EPI 7.8 Remove duplicates from a sorted list
d417.judge: Walk a pointer down the list; when the next node has the same value, skip it by relinking, otherwise advance.

d418.title: EPI 7.9 Implement cyclic right shift for singly linked lists
d418.judge: Find the tail and the length n in one walk, reduce k modulo n, link the tail to the head to close a ring, walk n - k steps to the new tail, and cut the ring after it.

d419.title: EPI 7.10 Implement even-odd merge
d419.judge: Keep an even tail and an odd tail; relink each next even node after the even tail and each next odd node after the odd tail, then link the even tail to the head of the odd nodes.

d420.title: EPI 7.11 Test whether a singly linked list is palindromic
d420.judge: Find the middle with a slow and a fast pointer, reverse the second half in place, and compare it node by node with the first half.

d421.title: EPI 7.12 Implement list pivoting
d421.judge: Three dummy heads with three tails for less, equal and greater; append each node to the tail of its group, end the greater group with None, and link the three groups in order.

d422.title: EPI 7.13 Add list-based integers
d422.judge: Walk both lists with a carry, add the two digits and the carry, append the digit sum % 10 as a new node after a dummy head and keep sum // 10 as the carry, and go on while either list or the carry remains.

d423.title: EPI 8.1 Implement a stack with max API
d423.judge: Each stack entry stores the value together with the largest value at or below it, computed at push time as max(x, the cached max of the entry below). max reads the cached max of the top entry, pop removes the top entry and returns its value, and empty tests the list.

d424.title: EPI 8.2 Evaluate RPN expressions
d424.judge: Split on ',' and keep a stack of values. A number token is pushed. An operator token pops the right operand first, then the left operand, applies the operator from a dict of functions and pushes the result. Division uses int(a / b) so that it rounds toward zero. The answer is the last value on the stack.

d425.title: EPI 8.3 Is a string well-formed?
d425.judge: Push each opening bracket. At a closing bracket, return False when the stack is empty or the popped bracket is not its matching opener, looked up in a closer-to-opener dict. At the end the string is well-formed only when the stack is empty.

d426.title: EPI 8.4 Normalize pathnames
d426.judge: Split the path on '/' and skip the empty names and '.'. Keep a stack of names: '..' pops the top name when the stack holds a real name, and is pushed otherwise, so a relative path keeps its leading '..'. Join the stack with '/' and add the leading '/' back for an absolute path.

d427.title: EPI 8.5 Compute buildings with a sunset view
d427.judge: Read the iterator once with enumerate and keep a stack of (index, height) with strictly decreasing heights: each new building pops every stacked building whose height is less than or equal to its own, then is pushed. The stack holds the buildings with a view, and the answer is their indices read from the top of the stack down.

d428.title: EPI 8.6 Compute binary tree nodes in order of increasing depth
d428.judge: Process the tree level by level: start with the list holding the root (none for an empty tree), append the values of the current level to the answer, and build the next level from the non-None left and right children of the current level, until a level is empty.

d429.title: EPI 8.7 Implement a circular queue
d429.judge: Store the values in a fixed list with a head index and a count. enqueue writes at (head + count) mod the list length; dequeue reads at head and moves head forward mod the list length. When count equals the list length, enqueue first rebuilds the list in queue order, values[head:] + values[:head], doubles its length and resets head to 0.

d430.title: EPI 8.8 Implement a queue using stacks
d430.judge: enqueue pushes onto an input stack. dequeue pops from an output stack; only when the output stack is empty does it move every value from the input stack to the output stack, which reverses their order so the oldest value is on top. Each value moves at most once.

d431.title: EPI 8.9 Implement a queue with max API
d431.judge: Keep the values in a deque and, beside it, a deque of candidates for the maximum whose values never increase from front to back. enqueue pops every candidate smaller than x from the back before appending x. dequeue pops the front value and also pops the front candidate when it equals that value. max returns the front candidate.

d432.title: EPI 9.1 Test if a binary tree is height-balanced
d432.judge: One post-order pass returns the height of each subtree upward, and an unbalanced subtree returns a sentinel such as -1 that every ancestor passes up unchanged.

d433.title: EPI 9.2 Test if a binary tree is symmetric
d433.judge: A helper takes two nodes at mirrored positions: both empty is True, one empty is False, else the values match and the helper holds for (left.left, right.right) and for (left.right, right.left).

d434.title: EPI 9.3 Compute the lowest common ancestor in a binary tree
d434.judge: A post-order search returns node0 or node1 when it meets either, else what its children found; the first node whose two children both return a node is the answer, and otherwise the non-empty child result goes up.

d435.title: EPI 9.4 Compute the LCA when nodes have parent pointers
d435.judge: Compute the depth of each node by walking parent pointers to the root, move the deeper node up by the difference, then move both up together until they are the same node.

d436.title: EPI 9.5 Sum the root-to-leaf paths in a binary tree
d436.judge: Pass the number read so far down the recursion as 2 * prefix + node.val; a leaf returns its number, an inner node returns the sum of its children's returns, an empty child returns 0.

d437.title: EPI 9.6 Find a root to leaf path with specified sum
d437.judge: Subtract the node weight from remaining_weight on the way down; a leaf answers remaining_weight == 0, and an inner node answers True when either child does.

d438.title: EPI 9.7 Implement an inorder traversal without recursion
d438.judge: An explicit stack and a current pointer: push and go left while the pointer is a node; when it is empty, pop, record the value, and move to the right child of the popped node.

d439.title: EPI 9.8 Compute the kth node in an inorder traversal
d439.judge: Walk down from the root with the size of the left subtree: go left when k is at most that size, stop at the node when k is that size plus 1, else subtract that size plus 1 from k and go right.

d440.title: EPI 9.9 Compute the successor
d440.judge: With a right child, the answer is the leftmost node of the right subtree. Without it, climb parent pointers while the node is a right child; the parent reached is the answer, None past the root.

d441.title: EPI 9.10 Implement an inorder traversal with constant space
d441.judge: Keep the previous node and the current node. Arriving from the parent, go left when there is a left child, else record and go right or up. Arriving from the left child, record and go right or up. Arriving from the right child, go up.

d442.title: EPI 9.11 Reconstruct a binary tree from traversal data
d442.judge: A dict maps each value to its index in inorder; the next preorder value is the root of the current inorder range [lo, hi), and the left and right parts of that range are built by recursion on index bounds.

d443.title: EPI 9.12 Reconstruct a binary tree from a preorder traversal with markers
d443.judge: A cursor over the list shared by all recursive calls: read the next entry, return None on a marker, else build the left subtree, then the right subtree, then the node.

d444.title: EPI 9.13 Compute the leaves of a binary tree
d444.judge: A recursion returns [node] for a leaf, [] for an empty tree, and the left result followed by the right result for an inner node.

d445.title: EPI 9.14 Compute the exterior of a binary tree
d445.judge: The root, then a pre-order pass over the left subtree with an is_boundary flag that stays on while the path takes left children (or the right child when no left child exists), then the mirror post-order pass over the right subtree; a node goes into the output when the flag is on or it is a leaf.

d446.title: EPI 9.15 Compute the right sibling tree
d446.judge: Go down the leftmost nodes level by level; on each level follow the next fields already set and set each child's next: left.next = right, right.next = node.next.left or None.

d447.title: EPI 10.1 Merge sorted files
d447.judge: A min-heap holds one entry per list: (value, list index, element index). Pop the smallest, append it, and push the next element of the same list.

d448.title: EPI 10.2 Sort an increasing-decreasing array
d448.judge: Cut A into runs where the direction changes, and reverse each decreasing run. Then merge the k sorted runs with a min-heap of (value, run index, element index).

d449.title: EPI 10.3 Sort an almost-sorted array
d449.judge: A min-heap of the first k elements. For each next element, push it and pop the smallest into the output (heappushpop). At the end, pop the rest of the heap.

d450.title: EPI 10.4 Compute the k closest stars
d450.judge: A max-heap by distance of at most k stars. Push each star and pop the farthest when the heap holds k + 1. The heap at the end is the answer.

d451.title: EPI 10.5 Compute the median of online data
d451.judge: Two heaps: a max-heap of the lower half and a min-heap of the upper half. Push into the lower half, move its top to the upper half, and move back when the upper half is larger. The median is the top of the lower half, or the mean of both tops when the sizes are equal.

d452.title: EPI 10.6 Compute the k largest elements in a max-heap
d452.judge: A max-heap of candidates holds (A[i], i), starting with the root. Pop k times; each pop adds the children 2i + 1 and 2i + 2 as candidates. A is only read.

d453.title: EPI 11.1 Search a sorted array for first occurrence of k
d453.judge: Binary search for the leftmost index whose value is not less than k (move lo past values less than k, else move hi to mid), then check that the index is in range and holds k.

d454.title: EPI 11.2 Search a sorted array for entry equal to its index
d454.judge: Binary search on the sign of A[mid] - mid: when A[mid] < mid go right, when A[mid] > mid go left, when they are equal return mid.

d455.title: EPI 11.3 Search a cyclically sorted array
d455.judge: Binary search that compares A[mid] with A[hi]: when A[mid] > A[hi] the smallest is to the right of mid, else it is at mid or to its left.

d456.title: EPI 11.4 Compute the integer square root
d456.judge: Binary search on the answer in [0, k] with an upper mid; keep mid when mid * mid <= k, else drop mid and everything above it.

d457.title: EPI 11.5 Compute the real square root
d457.judge: Bracket the root in [x, 1] when x < 1 and [1, x] otherwise, then bisect: keep the half where mid * mid is on the correct side of x until the interval is small relative to its upper end.

d458.title: EPI 11.6 Search in a 2D sorted array
d458.judge: Start at the top-right corner; when the entry equals x return True, when it is less than x go down a row, when it is greater go left a column.

d459.title: EPI 11.7 Find the min and max simultaneously
d459.judge: Take the entries in pairs; compare the two entries of a pair, then compare the smaller with the running minimum and the larger with the running maximum, with the first entry or pair as the start.

d460.title: EPI 11.8 Find the kth largest element
d460.judge: Pick a random pivot, partition the range so that values greater than the pivot come first, and keep only the side that holds position k - 1 until the pivot lands there.

d461.title: EPI 11.9 Find the missing IP address
d461.judge: First pass counts the values in each of the 2^16 buckets of the upper 16 bits and picks a bucket with fewer than 2^16 values; second pass marks the lower 16 bits of the values in that bucket and returns the first unmarked combination.

d462.title: EPI 11.10 Find the duplicate and missing elements
d462.judge: XOR every index and every value to get duplicate XOR missing, split by its lowest set bit and XOR the indices and values that have that bit to get one of the two, then a check of whether that value is in A tells which one it is.

d463.title: EPI 12.1 Test for palindromic permutations
d463.judge: Count each character, then count how many characters have an odd count. The answer is True when at most a single character has an odd count.

d464.title: EPI 12.2 Is an anonymous letter constructible?
d464.judge: Count the characters of letter_text only. Scan magazine_text and decrement the count of each character that the letter still needs, removing it at zero. Stop early when nothing is needed; the answer is whether nothing is needed at the end.

d465.title: EPI 12.3 Implement an ISBN cache
d465.judge: A single dict from isbn to price, kept in recency order: lookup and a repeated insert pop the key and put it back at the end. A new insert into a full cache first deletes the oldest key, the first key of the dict. erase pops the key and reports whether it was there.

d466.title: EPI 12.4 Compute the LCA, optimizing for close ancestors
d466.judge: Walk up from node0 and node1 at the same time, one step each in turn, and put every node passed into a hash set. The first node that a walk reaches and that is already in the set is the answer. A walk that has passed the root waits for the other.

d467.title: EPI 12.5 Find the nearest repeated entries in an array
d467.judge: A single pass with a dict from each word to the index where it was last seen. At each word, when it is in the dict, compare i minus its last index with the best distance; then record i. Return -1 when no distance was found.

d468.title: EPI 12.6 Find the smallest subarray covering all values
d468.judge: A sliding window with a count of each keyword inside it. Extend the right end by each word; while every keyword is inside, record the window when it is shorter than the best, then drop the left word and move the left end.

d469.title: EPI 12.7 Find smallest subarray sequentially covering all values
d469.judge: A dict from each keyword to its index, and for each keyword index j the latest start of a subarray that ends at the latest occurrence of keywords[j] and holds keywords[0..j] in order. At keywords[0] the start is the current index; at keywords[j] it is the stored start of keywords[j - 1]. At the last keyword, compare the subarray from that start with the best.

d470.title: EPI 12.8 Find the longest subarray with distinct entries
d470.judge: A dict of the last index of each value and a left end of the window. When the current value was last seen at or after the left end, move the left end past that index. Record the index, then compare the window length with the best.

d471.title: EPI 12.9 Find the length of a longest contained interval
d471.judge: Put the values in a set. Start a count only at a value x such that x - 1 is not in the set, and step up while the next integer is in the set. Each integer is stepped over at most a single time, which gives linear time.

d472.title: EPI 12.10 Compute all string decompositions
d472.judge: Count the words. For each start index, cut the substring of total length into word-length pieces, count the pieces and compare with the word counts. Collect the start indices that match, in increasing order.

d473.title: EPI 12.11 Test the Collatz conjecture
d473.judge: Every integer below the current start is already known to reach 1, so the walk from each start stops as soon as it drops below that start. Even starts drop at the first step and can be skipped. A set of the values on the current walk detects a cycle, which is the False case.

d474.title: EPI 13.1 Compute the intersection of two sorted arrays
d474.judge: A pointer into each list. Advance the pointer at the smaller value; on equal values, append the value when it differs from the last appended value, then advance both.

d475.title: EPI 13.2 Merge two sorted arrays
d475.judge: Fill A from its last index down. Read pointers start at the last entry of each sorted part; at each write position, copy the larger of the two values and move that read pointer. Writing from the back never overwrites an unread entry of A.

d476.title: EPI 13.3 Computing the h-index
d476.judge: Sort the citations in decreasing order. The paper at index i has at least i + 1 citations exactly for the first h indices, so the h-index is the count of indices i with a citation count greater than i.

d477.title: EPI 13.4 Remove first-name duplicates
d477.judge: Sort A so that equal first names are next to each other. A write index keeps the next free position: copy an entry there when its first name differs from the last written entry. Delete the entries after the write index.

d478.title: EPI 13.5 Smallest nonconstructible value
d478.judge: Sort A. Keep the largest value r such that every integer from 1 to r is a subset sum of the entries seen so far. When the next entry is at most r + 1, every value up to r plus that entry becomes reachable; when it is larger, r + 1 is the answer.

d479.title: EPI 13.6 Render a calendar
d479.judge: Turn each event into a start point and a finish point, sorted by time with a start before a finish at the same time. Sweep the points, adding 1 at a start and subtracting 1 at a finish, and keep the largest running count.

d480.title: EPI 13.7 Merging intervals
d480.judge: The intervals that end before the new interval starts stay as they are, and so do the intervals that start after it ends. Every interval between them overlaps the new interval and is merged into it by the smallest left end and the largest right end. Return the three parts in order.

d481.title: EPI 13.8 Compute the union of intervals
d481.judge: Sort by left end, with a closed left end before an open left end at the same value. Compare each interval with the last interval of the result: it joins when its left end is below that right end, or equal to it with at least a single end closed. A joined interval extends the right end when its right end is larger, or equal and closed.

d482.title: EPI 13.9 Partitioning and sorting an array with many repeated entries
d482.judge: Count each age and give each age a block of positions with a next free position. For each age, look at its next free position: an entry of that age advances the position, and an entry of another age is swapped into the next free position of its own age. Each swap puts an entry in its final block.

d483.title: EPI 13.10 Team photo day - 1
d483.judge: Sort both teams and pair them by rank. A valid placement exists exactly when each player of team0 is shorter than the team1 player of the same rank.

d484.title: EPI 13.11 Implement a fast sorting algorithm for lists
d484.judge: Merge sort on the list. Find the middle with a slow and a fast pointer, cut the list there, and sort each half recursively. Merge the halves behind a dummy head, taking from the left half on equal values so that the sort is stable.

d485.title: EPI 13.12 Compute a salary threshold
d485.judge: Sort the salaries and keep the sum of the salaries below the current index. At index i, if that sum plus the current salary times the number of remaining people reaches the target, the cap is the target minus that sum, divided by the number of remaining people. Return -1.0 when no index reaches the target.

d486.title: EPI 14.1 Test if a binary tree satisfies the BST property
d486.judge: A recursion passes an allowed range [low, high] down: the node key must be inside it, the left child gets [low, key] and the right child gets [key, high], starting from minus and plus infinity.

d487.title: EPI 14.2 Find the first key greater than a given value in a BST
d487.judge: One walk down from the root: when the key is greater than k, record the node and go left; otherwise go right. The last recorded node is the answer.

d488.title: EPI 14.3 Find the k largest elements in a BST
d488.judge: A reverse inorder walk (right subtree, node, left subtree) that appends keys and stops every call once the result holds k keys.

d489.title: EPI 14.4 Compute the LCA in a BST
d489.judge: Walk down from the root: go left while both keys are smaller than the node key, go right while both are larger; the first node whose key is between s.val and b.val is the answer.

d490.title: EPI 14.5 Reconstruct a BST from traversal data
d490.judge: A shared index into preorder_sequence and a recursion with an allowed range (low, high): when the next key is outside the range return None, else make the node, advance the index, build the left with (low, key) and the right with (key, high).

d491.title: EPI 14.6 Find the closest entries in three sorted arrays
d491.judge: A min-heap holds the current entry of each array and the largest current entry is kept apart; pop the smallest, update the best difference, push the next entry from the same array, and stop when an array runs out.

d492.title: EPI 14.7 Enumerate extended integers
d492.judge: Build the answer list in order with two indices into it: the candidates are answer[i] + 1 and answer[j] + sqrt(2); append the smaller and advance every index whose candidate equals it, so no value is added twice.

d493.title: EPI 14.8 Build a minimum height BST from a sorted array
d493.judge: A recursion on index bounds [lo, hi): the middle entry becomes the root, the left half builds the left subtree and the right half builds the right subtree.

d494.title: EPI 14.9 Test if three BST nodes are totally ordered
d494.judge: Search from both candidates toward middle at the same time, one step each; stop when a search reaches middle or the other candidate, or both searches end. When one reaches middle first, search from middle for the other candidate.

d495.title: EPI 14.10 The range lookup problem
d495.judge: An inorder walk that goes left only when left < key, records the key when left <= key <= right, and goes right only when key < right.

d496.title: EPI 14.11 Add credits
d496.judge: A dict of credit minus a global offset per client, an offset that add_all increases, and a max-heap of (stored credit, client) with lazy deletion: max pops heap tops whose stored credit no longer matches the dict.

d497.title: EPI 15.1 The Towers of Hanoi problem
d497.judge: Recursion on the ring count: move the top n - 1 rings to the spare peg, move the largest ring to the target peg, then move the n - 1 rings from the spare peg onto it. Zero rings need no move.

d498.title: EPI 15.2 Compute all mnemonics for a phone number
d498.judge: A recursive walk over the digit positions with a partial string: at position i each character of the key of digit i is appended, the walk recurses on i + 1, and the character is removed after. A partial string of full length is copied into the result.

d499.title: EPI 15.3 Generate all nonattacking placements of n-Queens
d499.judge: Rows are filled in order, one queen per row. Sets of the used columns and of the two diagonal keys (row + column and row - column) tell in O(1) whether a column is free; they are updated before the recursive call and restored after it.

d500.title: EPI 15.4 Generate permutations
d500.judge: A recursive build of the ordering with a used flag per index (or a swap of A[i] with each later entry): each unused entry is appended, the build recurses, then the entry is removed and its flag cleared. An ordering of full length is copied out.

d501.title: EPI 15.5 Generate the power set
d501.judge: Each recursive call records a copy of the current subset, then for each index from its start index on appends that entry, recurses with start = index + 1 and removes it. The bit-mask form, one subset per integer 0 to 2^n - 1, is also accepted.

d502.title: EPI 15.6 Generate all subsets of size k
d502.judge: Start-index recursion over 1 to n that stops at size k: each call tries each next number from its start, recurses with that number + 1 as the start and removes it. The loop stops early when too few numbers remain to reach size k.

d503.title: EPI 15.7 Generate strings of matched parens
d503.judge: Recursion on the counts of '(' and ')' placed so far: '(' may be added while fewer than num_pairs are placed, ')' only while there are fewer ')' than '('. A string is recorded when the ')' count reaches num_pairs.

d504.title: EPI 15.8 Generate palindromic decompositions
d504.judge: Recursion on the start index of the next piece: for each end, when text[start:end] is a palindrome it is appended, the recursion continues from end, and the piece is removed after. Reaching the end of text records a copy of the pieces.

d505.title: EPI 15.9 Generate binary trees
d505.judge: For each size i of the left subtree from 0 to num_nodes - 1, every tree of i nodes is combined with every tree of num_nodes - 1 - i nodes under a new root. The base case of 0 nodes returns [None].

d506.title: EPI 15.10 Implement a Sudoku solver
d506.judge: Sets per row, per column and per box are seeded from the given digits, and a clash among the given digits returns False at once. The blanks are listed and filled in order; a digit goes into the three sets and the cell before the recursive call and comes out after the call fails.

d507.title: EPI 15.11 Compute a Gray code
d507.judge: Reflection: the code for b bits is the code for b - 1 bits followed by the same list in reverse with bit b - 1 set. The closed form i ^ (i >> 1) for i from 0 to 2^num_bits - 1 is also accepted.

d508.title: EPI 16.1 Count the number of score combinations
d508.judge: A table ways[s] of the number of combinations for each score s, with ways[0] = 1. The play scores are the outer loop and the score the inner loop going up, so each combination is counted once whatever the order of its plays.

d509.title: EPI 16.2 Compute the Levenshtein distance
d509.judge: A table over prefixes: cell (i, j) is the distance from A[:i] to B[:j]. Equal last characters copy the diagonal cell; otherwise the cell is 1 + the min of the diagonal (replace), the cell above (delete) and the cell to the left (insert). The first row and column are 0 to len; two rolling rows are enough.

d510.title: EPI 16.3 Count the number of ways to traverse a 2D array
d510.judge: The count of a cell is the count of the cell above plus the count of the cell to the left, with 1 along the first row and the first column. One row of length min(n, m) is updated in place, row by row.

d511.title: EPI 16.4 Compute the binomial coefficients
d511.judge: Pascal's rule C(i, j) = C(i - 1, j - 1) + C(i - 1, j), filled row by row in one array of length k + 1, with j going down so that each cell still reads the previous row.

d512.title: EPI 16.5 Search for a sequence in a 2D array
d512.judge: The state is (cell, position in pattern) and each state is decided once: a memo on (i, j, offset), or a forward pass that keeps the set of cells where the prefix of pattern read so far can end and moves to the neighbours that hold the next entry. An empty pattern returns True.

d513.title: EPI 16.6 The knapsack problem
d513.judge: The state is (number of items considered, remaining capacity). The bottom-up form keeps one array best[c] over capacities and updates it for each item with c going down from capacity to the weight of the item, so each item is used at most once.

d514.title: EPI 16.7 Building a search index for domains
d514.judge: For each prefix length, record whether the prefix splits into words and the length of its last word: a prefix of length end works when a shorter working prefix is followed by a dictionary word that ends at end. The words are read back from the end of domain along the recorded lengths.

d515.title: EPI 16.8 Find the minimum weight path in a triangle
d515.judge: Bottom-up from the last row: each entry becomes its own value plus the smaller of its two children in the row below, kept in one row array; the answer is the entry left at the top. Top-down with the min over the last row is also accepted.

d516.title: EPI 16.9 Pick up coins for maximum gain
d516.judge: The state is the subarray coins[i:j]. The best take of the player to move is the total of the subarray minus the smaller of the best takes of the other player on the two subarrays left after taking either end coin. The table is filled for increasing lengths, or memoized on (i, j).

d517.title: EPI 16.10 Count the number of moves to climb stairs
d517.judge: ways[h] is the sum of ways[h - s] for s from 1 to maximum_step with s <= h, and ways[0] = 1, filled for h from 1 to top. A sliding sum of the last maximum_step entries is also accepted.

d518.title: EPI 16.11 The pretty printing problem
d518.judge: best[i] is the least messiness of the first i words. For each i, the last line takes words j to i - 1 for j going down while they fit, and best[i] is the min over those j of best[j] + (free characters)^2. The scan stops when the line no longer fits, which gives the line_length factor.

d519.title: EPI 16.12 Find the longest nondecreasing subsequence
d519.judge: ends[i] is the length of the longest nondecreasing subsequence that ends at A[i]: 1 plus the max of ends[j] over j < i with A[j] <= A[i]. The answer is the max over i. The O(n log n) form with bisect_right on the smallest tails is also accepted.

d520.title: EPI 17.1 Compute an optimum assignment of tasks
d520.judge: Sort the durations, then pair the shortest with the longest, the second shortest with the second longest, and so on inward. An exchange argument shows that any other pairing has a largest sum at least as big.

d521.title: EPI 17.2 Schedule to minimize waiting time
d521.judge: Serve the customers in increasing order of service time. Each service time adds to the wait of every customer after it, so the total is the sum of each time multiplied by the number of customers served after it.

d522.title: EPI 17.3 The interval covering problem
d522.judge: Sort the intervals by right endpoint. Keep the last point placed; when an interval starts after that point, place a new point at its right endpoint and count it.

d523.title: EPI 17.4 The 3-sum problem
d523.judge: Sort A. For each entry a, run the two-sum check for t - a with two pointers from both ends of A, where i <= j so an index can repeat: move the left pointer up when the sum is too small and the right pointer down when it is too large.

d524.title: EPI 17.5 Find the majority element
d524.judge: Keep a candidate and a count. When the count is 0, the next string becomes the candidate. A string equal to the candidate adds 1, any other string subtracts 1. The candidate at the end is the majority.

d525.title: EPI 17.6 The gasup problem
d525.judge: Walk the cities once from city 0 and keep the running gas balance 20 * gas[i] - dist[i] in miles. The city after the point where the balance is lowest is ample, because from there every partial sum is at least 0.

d526.title: EPI 17.7 Compute the maximum water trapped by a pair of vertical lines
d526.judge: Start with the two outer lines and record their water. Move the pointer at the shorter line inward, because every pair that keeps the shorter line and is narrower holds less water. Stop when the pointers meet.

d527.title: EPI 17.8 Compute the largest rectangle under the skyline
d527.judge: Keep a stack of indices with increasing heights, and add a height 0 at the end. When a building is not taller than the top, pop the top: its rectangle spans from the index below it on the stack to the current index, both excluded.

d528.title: EPI 18.1 Search a maze
d528.judge: Search from s with an explicit stack or a queue over the open neighbours, and record the parent of each cell when it is first seen. When e comes off the stack, follow the parents back to s and reverse the list.

d529.title: EPI 18.2 Paint a Boolean matrix
d529.judge: Read the value of (x, y), flip it, and put the cell in a queue. Take cells from the queue and flip each in-bounds neighbour that still has the old value, then add it to the queue. A flipped cell no longer matches, so no cell is visited twice.

d530.title: EPI 18.3 Compute enclosed regions
d530.judge: Start a search from every "W" cell on the border and mark each "W" cell it reaches. Then set every unmarked "W" cell to "B" and turn the marked cells back to "W".

d531.title: EPI 18.4 Deadlock detection
d531.judge: Run a DFS from each unvisited vertex with three states: not visited, on the current path, and finished. An edge to a vertex on the current path is a cycle. A vertex is set to finished when its DFS returns, so an edge to a finished vertex is not a cycle.

d532.title: EPI 18.5 Clone a graph
d532.judge: Keep a map from each original vertex to its copy. Traverse from graph with a queue: for each edge v -> w, make the copy of w the first time w is seen, and append the copy of w to the neighbors of the copy of v. Return the copy of graph.

d533.title: EPI 18.6 Making wired connections
d533.judge: Start a BFS from each vertex with no side yet and give it side 0. Each new neighbour gets the other side. An edge between two vertices with the same side means the split is impossible.

d534.title: EPI 18.7 Transform one string to another
d534.judge: BFS from s with the distance of each string. The neighbours of a string are the strings made by changing one position to each of the 26 letters that are in D and not seen yet. Return the distance when t comes off the queue.

d535.title: EPI 18.8 Team photo day - 2
d535.judge: Find the longest path in a DAG. Process the vertices in topological order, with Kahn's in-degree queue or a memoized DFS. For each edge v -> w, the longest path that ends at w is at least the longest path that ends at v plus 1. The answer is the largest of these values.

d537.title: Odd Sum Subarrays
d537.judge: A subarray sum is the difference of two prefix sums, and the empty prefix 0 is one of them. The sum is odd when the two prefix sums have different parity. Count the odd prefix sums; the even prefix sums are the rest plus the empty prefix; the answer is the product of the two counts.
